name: Real-time / online feature stores (independent)
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Three independent (non-hyperscaler-bundled) feature stores define this segment as of May 2026: (1) Chalk - real-time feature platform, proprietary cloud SaaS, raised $50M Series A at $500M valuation in May 2025 (led by Felicis), positions itself as 'real-time data platform for AI inference', sub-5ms feature retrieval, named customers Whatnot, Apartment List, Medely, Doppel, Sunrun, Socure, Found, iwoca; Compute Engine translates Python features to C++/Rust pipelines. (2) Feast - Apache-2.0, Linux Foundation AI/Data Foundation project (originated at Gojek, joined LF AI in 2020), Red Hat blog endorsement (May 2025), recently joined the PyTorch Ecosystem; online store is BYO (Redis, DynamoDB, Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake). Feast is a fetch/serving layer, not a compute layer - upstream Spark/Flink/dbt is expected to compute aggregates. (3) Hopsworks - AGPL-v3 open-core, RonDB-backed online tier (sub-ms p99, SIGMOD 2024 paper claims 10x lower p99 vs SageMaker/Vertex), enterprise edition with HA + security + UI behind a license. Tecton (acq. Databricks Aug 22 2025) and Fennel (acq. Databricks Apr 17 2025) are no longer standalone and have rolled into the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform / Agent Bricks (see segment X1). Adjacent open-source projects: Featureform (acquired by Redis Oct 9 2025, now 'Redis Feature Form'), Tacnode (newer entrant), Alibaba FeatHub.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Within the independent online-FS-for-ranking/fraud niche specifically (the segment beava overlaps with): Chalk owns the high-throughput live-commerce/marketplace recsys reference (Whatnot 300M+ features/sec, P99 100 ms, sub-5ms Apartment List, Medely healthcare-staffing real-time pricing/matching with documented ~$800k/yr revenue lift on a single charge-rate model and 24h-batch-to-real-time migration off Redis). Feast holds the open-source default position with broad Spark/Flink/dbt-fed deployments at PayPal-style risk teams (Linux Foundation 'F'inOps governance, ~6k GitHub stars, joined PyTorch Ecosystem in 2025-2026). Hopsworks holds the EU/on-prem 'AI lakehouse with first-class feature store' position with public fraud-online/fraud-batch tutorials and a Feldera+Hopsworks real-time fraud reference; SIGMOD 2024 paper headlines 10x p99 vs hyperscalers. Funding/M&A 2025-2026: Chalk $50M Series A May 2025 (Felicis lead, $500M valuation, prior seed from General Catalyst/Unusual/Xfund); Tecton acquired by Databricks Aug 22 2025 (prior $900M valuation, $160M total raised); Fennel acquired by Databricks Apr 17 2025 (Rust real-time engine, ex-Meta/Google Brain team); Featureform acquired by Redis Oct 9 2025 and re-launched as 'Redis Feature Form' in Apr 2026. The independent segment has contracted to three viable players (Chalk, Feast, Hopsworks) in roughly one year.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed - this is the segment's defining buyer filter. Feast is Apache-2.0 (the cleanest license posture, Linux Foundation governance, no enterprise upsell, Red Hat-blessed). Hopsworks is AGPL-v3 open-core (community edition is AGPL which is a non-starter for most enterprise legal teams per Google's published AGPL Policy, and Enterprise Edition is paid - a real open-core split). Chalk is proprietary closed-source SaaS (no community OSS option). Tecton was proprietary SaaS, now Databricks-internal. Beava's Apache-2.0 posture is at parity with Feast and materially cleaner than Hopsworks/Chalk for procurement-conscious buyers.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium-to-High for this segment. The Databricks acquisitions of Tecton (Aug 2025) and Fennel (Apr 2025) plus the Redis acquisition of Featureform (Oct 2025) collapsed roughly half of the prior independent feature-store market into hyperscaler bundles within 6 months. Any Databricks customer can now provision Tecton-backed feature serving via Agent Bricks without a separate procurement; any Redis Enterprise customer will get Redis Feature Form bundled. SageMaker Feature Store (online on DynamoDB), Vertex AI Feature Store (Bigtable), and Databricks Online Feature Store/Lakebase are already credible 'good-enough' alternatives bundled into existing hyperscaler subscriptions. The remaining independent buyers - those who explicitly do NOT want a Databricks/AWS/GCP lock-in - are Chalk's, Feast's, Hopsworks's, and beava's joint addressable market. This is the highest-bundling-pressure segment beava competes in.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Independent feature stores split sharply on ingestion model. Feast assumes upstream Spark/Flink/dbt computes features and writes them to the online store on a schedule (materialise-and-push), with Kafka/Kinesis the dominant streaming-input path. Hopsworks similarly assumes Spark/Flink materialisation into RonDB. Chalk owns the compute side (Python features -> C++/Rust pipelines) but expects Kafka/Kinesis or direct application writes for streaming-input. Tecton historically required a Spark/Flink pipeline for batch features plus a 'StreamFeatureView' for Kafka. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 + framed-TCP :8081 (JSON or msgpack) push-on-event model is materially differentiated - it accepts webhook-style ingestion and mobile-SDK direct push WITHOUT a Kafka broker hop, which Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks do not. This is a fit for mid-market buyers without a streaming platform team (the Medely/Apartment-List shape) and a friction for tier-1 buyers already standardised on Kafka who expect a consumer-side connector.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Independent feature stores in this segment are scorer-agnostic by design and feed (a) external rules engines (Drools, FEEL, in-house DSL, Snowflake SQL functions, Chalk's own resolver DSL), (b) ML scorers (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, ONNX, in-house Python, transformer-based sequence models). Production deployments routinely use both in parallel - rules for hard policy thresholds (Amazon/Walmart/eBay performance-standard cutoffs, Uber/DoorDash acceptance-rate cutoffs) and ML for graded scoring. Beava plays the same role: a feature substrate under both, decoupled from the scorer. This is structurally the same coupling as Feast/Tecton/Chalk/Hopsworks.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Five concrete reasons a buyer in this segment would pick beava over Chalk/Feast/Hopsworks today: (1) Single binary collapses the (Kafka + Flink + Redis + Feast) or (Spark + RonDB + Hopsworks) two-or-more-box norm into one process - meaningful for ML platform teams that do not want to run a streaming-platform team. Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks all expect upstream Spark/Flink to compute aggregates; beava bakes 50+ aggregation primitives into the server itself. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives baked into the server (count, sum, mean, n_unique HLL, CMS top-K, t-digest quantile, velocity, distance, last-N) vs Feast which is explicitly a fetch-layer, not a compute-layer. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP batch_get from the published benchmarks is at parity with Chalk's sub-5ms / Tecton's published 0.8ms / Hopsworks's 1.93ms-avg-3ms-p99 100-row batch and materially faster than Vertex AI FS's ~30ms server-side. (4) Push-on-event ingestion over HTTP/JSON + framed-TCP without a Kafka broker requirement - Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks assume Kafka or a managed CDC pipe. The mobile-SDK direct push and webhook patterns work natively against beava. (5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core upsell and no acquisition risk - cleaner than Hopsworks (AGPL/Enterprise split) and Chalk (closed source SaaS), and a structural hedge against the Databricks/Redis bundling pressure that took out Tecton/Fennel/Featureform.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps that block adoption in this segment today, derived from use cases 18a/18b/10/21: (1) No TLS/auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 in v0 - every managed independent competitor (Chalk SaaS, Tecton-now-Databricks, Hopsworks Enterprise) ships TLS + IAM out of the box; this is a procurement non-starter for ML platform teams in cloud VPCs. (2) No in-process sharding - Whatnot/DoorDash/Instacart-scale state cannot fit on one box; the single-tenant ceiling is ~684k EPS write and ~100-200 GB hot state. Chalk/Hopsworks/Tecton all scale horizontally. (3) No multi-region active-active replication - global ranking/authorisation paths require cross-region online stores; Databricks Online Feature Store and SageMaker FS ship this; beava does not. (4) No first-class offline/online parity story - beava is online-only, so the buyer must own offline consistency (Snowflake/Databricks/BigQuery) themselves and guarantee that offline aggregations match the online @bv.table definitions. Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks/Chalk all market 'point-in-time correctness' as a headline feature. (5) No materialisation-from-warehouse - beava expects events pushed in; Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks accept 'compute this feature in Spark nightly, write to online store' as a first-class pattern. (6) No multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs - ML platform teams hosting multiple risk/ranking teams cannot isolate them. (7) No SDK ergonomics for tabular ML idioms - Feast/Tecton ship `get_online_features(entity_rows=DataFrame, feature_view=...)` returning a DataFrame; beava's get/batch_get is lower-level. (8) No feature monitoring / drift detection - Tecton/Hopsworks publish per-feature counters, distribution sketches, drift webhooks as core capability. (9) No on-demand feature transformations at request time (Tecton's 'On-Demand Feature Views', Chalk's 'resolvers') - these are deterministic functions of the request payload and Plaid Signal/Coinbase explicitly call them out. (10) No managed/hosted offering - the buyer must operate the box themselves; Chalk/Tecton-now-Databricks/Hopsworks Serverless all ship managed.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo. Closing the procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS + auth + namespace ACLs, items 1 and 6 above) is 1-3 months. Closing the differentiating-feature gaps (in-process sharding, materialisation-from-warehouse, get_online_features DataFrame SDK, point-in-time-correctness contract, on-demand resolvers, basic feature monitoring, items 2/4/5/7/8/9) is another 3-9 months on top. A managed/hosted offering (item 10) is a separate quarter+ of GTM and ops work, but is not strictly required for design-partner deployments with self-hosted ML platform teams - which is the realistic 'first credible 18b/18a buyer' shape.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Mixed. Beava-side: zero publicly named users in this segment, no published Whatnot/Apartment-List-equivalent case study, beava.dev landing page positions as 'real-time features without heavy infrastructure'. Repo evidence: python/beava/demos/fraud/ (schema.json, events.jsonl, raw-event-ingestion + aggregation covering 18a/fraud shape) and python/beava/demos/ecommerce/ (PageView/AddToCart/Purchase keyed on user_id/sku, the canonical 18b recsys event shape) plus crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json and workloads/fraud.rs are runnable, but the explicit 'plug beava into XGBoost/LightGBM, serve N features in one batch_get' notebook (the Feast/Tecton/SageMaker demo shape) is not yet shipped, and no recsys-rerank bench config exists. Competitor-side validation that the segment shape is real: Chalk's Whatnot/Apartment-List/Medely public case studies, Tecton's 0.8 ms / 100M txn/day / 40% false-positive-reduction fraud reference (Coinbase, Plaid Signal), Hopsworks SIGMOD 2024 paper with 10x p99 vs SageMaker/Vertex, Feast's Linux Foundation governance and PyTorch Ecosystem inclusion. Beava knows who the buyer is (ML platform team at mid-market fintech / regional marketplace / healthcare-staffing platform; design-partner shape) but does not yet have proof points in this segment.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete - credible play with 3-9 months of focused engineering on TLS/auth/multi-tenancy/sharding plus a published recsys-rerank and online-FS-for-fraud demo with a paired Python notebook against XGBoost. Beava's wedge (single binary + 60 primitives + Apache-2.0 + sub-ms batch_get + no-Kafka push) is real and differentiated against the three remaining independent incumbents, but the hyperscaler-bundling pressure (X1) is increasing and the segment timer is shorter than it was in 2024. The realistic play is a design-partner with one mid-market ML platform team in fraud/risk (18a) or live-commerce/marketplace recsys (18b) where Tecton-now-Databricks lock-in is unappealing and Chalk's SaaS pricing is the friction. Avoid pitching tier-1 buyers (Whatnot/DoorDash-scale) until in-process sharding ships.
